why: p23 thins to near-silence at 0:26 before the full ensemble arrives 13 dB louder, a real arrival, while p08 stays within about 2 dB from 0:13 on and only its 2:14 dropout gives any relief.
p10's muffled late-night keys and the near-empty breakdown at bar 29 pull you in more than p21's wall-to-wall trap loop, although p21's dropout and beat switch at 2:47 are the stronger single moment.
p06's filtered preview bursting to full level at 0:10 and its sighing lament descent are melancholy and immersive, while p25's sax-led band groove from 0:40 is warm and nostalgic rather than cool.
Both are one-level game-style synth rushes, but p22's full band slamming in at 0:17 after a filtered intro and its F#-major lift at 2:09 hit harder than p08's gradual piano-to-band entry at 0:26.

p06's wistful guitar loop with drumless floating stretches at 0:58 and 1:46 fits the moody, breathing ideal, while p22 hammers one bright three-chord loop at full volume, with only a 7-second breakdown at 2:21.
p23 builds from near-silence to a crashing climax at 0:27 and 1:08, while p09 is sunny, focus-music arpeggios that just repeat and fade at 2:03.
p24's band crashing in heavy and dark at 0:21 after a sparse clean intro is the kind of physical arrival this listener loves, while p08 is an uplifting action-game rush that stays at one level.
p25 has a bittersweet minor-to-major lift and a drumless middle at 1:15, while p09 is bright, pastel, new-age looping that restates itself and fades.
p07's low-passed intro opening into the full breakbeat groove at 0:21 gives a cool, hypnotic arrival, while p21's sad trap loop sits flat until its beat switch at 2:47.
p06's melancholy guitar sigh and slow unresolved ending pull you in, while p23's music-box intro and heroic climax loop from 1:08 are the cinematic-build type that lands in the middle.
p10's dark, hypnotic trip-hop, with its bright lift at 0:54 and near-silent breakdown at bar 29, is cooler and breathes more than p22's loud, bright synth loop that barely lets up.
p24's crash-in at 0:21 is a bigger arrival, but its menacing D-Eb grind and unchanging wall lean toward relentless riffing, while p10 stays moody and immersive and drops almost to nothing at bar 29.
p24's band crashing in heavy at 0:21 is powerful, but its grinding riff wall barely breathes for two minutes, while p06 keeps a sad, immersive mood and floats in drumless passages at 0:58 and 1:46.
p10's late-night trip-hop mood and bar-29 breakdown are cool and immersive, while p23 goes from a delicate chiming intro to a heroic climax loop from 1:08, a middle-tier cinematic build.
p25 goes from hazy intro to a band entry at 0:40 and then a drumless development at 1:15, giving real dynamics, while p08 is an uplifting game rush held within 2 dB almost throughout.
p07's moody Bbmaj7-Am7 groove landing out of a filtered intro at 0:21 is cool and hypnotic, while p23's music-box opening and heroic climax at 1:08 are more theatrical than immersive.
p22 at least drives, slamming in at 0:17 with a bright lift at 2:09, while p09 is gentle, sunny, focus-music arpeggios with almost no change.
p24's heavy, sad band crashing in at 0:21 after a clean intro is a bigger physical arrival than p07's filter-opening drop at 0:21, and p07's second half just repeats its club loop.
p07's cool, slightly dark two-chord groove with its stripped breakdown at 2:01 pulls you in, while p22's loud, bright arpeggio loop from 0:17 is energetic but flat.
p07's muffled intro dropping into a tight, moody groove at 0:21 feels cooler than p25's warm, nostalgic band groove from 0:40, though p25's drumless middle at 1:15 breathes more.
p06's wistful guitar descent and drumless floating interludes at 1:46 and 2:43 are more immersive than p21's hot, flat trap loop, whose only real lift is the beat switch at 2:47.
p24 has a sad, heavy crash-in at 0:21, while p09 is sunny, pastel, focus-music arpeggio looping that fades at 2:03.
p10's dark, hypnotic late-night keys and near-silent breakdown at bar 29 are cooler than p25's warm, nostalgic sax-and-bass groove from 0:40.
p21's sad, glossy loop, with a dropout at 2:40 before the beat switch, is moodier than p08's uplifting action-game arpeggios, which hold one level from 0:26 on.
p21's moody trap loop, with drums crashing in at 0:16 and a beat switch at 2:47, beats p09's gentle, sunny arpeggio loop, which just fades out at 2:03.
